name: Folded Pass
description: The surrealists' folded-paper game (the surrealists called it Exquisite Corpse, others call it Consequences), built for a classroom. Each sentence passes through six hands, one word per hand, nobody seeing what came before: adjective, noun, adverb, verb, adjective, noun. Every sentence returns to the student who started it, assembled, and then the class hears some out loud. Any class size works: with fewer than six students a paper comes around twice, still blind. No points, no winners, no wrong answers.
tagline: Perfect for vocabulary practice, parts of speech, creative writing warm-ups, or pure play.

theme.label: Theme
theme.helper: A nudge for word choices: 'the ocean', 'ancient Rome', 'our vocabulary list'. Leave the default for pure surrealism.

wordTimer.label: Seconds per word
wordTimer.helper: How long each word round stays open. Short keeps the folds moving; 25 is plenty for one word.

template.name: Folded Pass
template.description: A blind pass-and-write sentence built with the Folded Pass recipe, six hands and nobody saw the whole thing coming.

intro.message:
FOLDED PASS

The surrealists' folded-paper game. We build sentences together, but here's the fold: each of you adds ONE word without seeing any of the words before yours.

Six words, six folds. At the end, the sentence you started comes back to you, finished by hands that never saw it. Nobody knows what any sentence says yet. Not even the people writing it.

word-1.prompt:
Word 1 of 6. Write one ADJECTIVE, a describing word (sleepy, ancient, sparkling, suspicious).

Theme: ${theme}

unfold.message:
Pencils down. Every paper unfolds at once.

The sentence each of you started is about to come back, finished by classmates who never saw it. Read yours quietly first. Then some go up on the class screen for everyone.

share.message: Some of the sentences, one at a time. Read each one out loud.

end.message: Six hands, no plan, and somehow it's poetry. The surrealists would be proud.
